Shopping for a W463 G 500? The year matters more than the mileage.

2002–04: early US trucks have the electrical gremlins. Seat motors, window regulators, door-lock and transfer-case actuators.
2005–08: the sweet spot. Specialists say the faults were mostly gone by 2005–06.

And mind the gearbox: the seven-speed 7G-Tronic arrived with June 2006 production, the 2007 model year in the US. 2005–06 trucks keep the simpler five-speed. How to tell which one you're looking at is in our G 500 guide at boxytrucks.com.

Whatever the year, check for rust where nobody cleans: the tailgate's lower edge, door bottoms, sills and the rear frame tubes.

Mine's a 2007, the first US year with the 7-speed.

The argument that never ends on IH8MUD: 80 Series or 100 Series?

Buy the 80 if you want solid axles, factory front and rear lockers, and the simplest Land Cruiser to fix in a driveway.

Buy the 100 if you tow, drive long highway stretches or carry a family, and want V8 power, the five-speed (2003 on) and a quieter cabin.

The full head-to-head, with specs, what breaks and what they cost now, is at boxytrucks.com/compare.

Wrangler or Bronco? For most buyers, the Bronco: its independent front suspension makes it the better truck to drive every day.

But the Wrangler Rubicon still has what rock crawlers want: a solid front axle and a 4:1 transfer case to build on. And used two-doors start cheaper.

Buy the Wrangler if you crawl rocks. Buy the Bronco if you spend more time on pavement and fast dirt than in boulders, or want factory 35s.

The new boxes: Defender, Grenadier or G-Class?

The Defender is the best all-rounder and by far the cheapest used. The Grenadier is the traditional one, ladder frame and beam axles, for people who like to know how things work. The G-Class gives you three lockers and a ladder frame inside a luxury car, at luxury-car prices.

Every Land Cruiser generation has a year to look for.

FJ40, 1976 on: front disc brakes on top of the 2F and four-speed. Owners call 1978 the coveted year.
80 Series, 1993–97: the 4.5 L 1FZ-FE six, bigger brakes and optional front and rear lockers.
100 Series, 2003–07: the five-speed automatic. Skip 1998–99 if you wheel hard; the two-pinion front diff is the weak one.
200 Series, 2013 on: the facelift made Multi-Terrain Select, Multi-Terrain Monitor and Off-Road Turn Assist standard.

Every generation, with the years to avoid too, is at boxytrucks.com.
